accessNotes: The SvelteKit pages render a 'content blocked - only accessible with your Michelin credentials' login wall, but the public __data.json payloads for each route contain the page rich-text (design guidelines, bar/line/donut/bubble component guidance) and image upload paths, which were read. Exact palette hexes, fonts and Chart.js defaults come from the public npm packages @michelin/theme 12.1.0 (_data-viz-colors.scss, _typography.scss) and @michelin/charts 12.1.0 (Angular wrapper around Chart.js 4).
summary: Enterprise product-UI design system for Angular dashboards. Charts are Chart.js 4 rendered via @michelin/charts in Noto Sans, with semi-transparent fills (60% for bars/pies), faint 10%-black gridlines, point-style legends, and cards on a light-grey dashboard background. Guidance is pragmatic do/don't: sorted bars from 0, horizontal bars instead of rotated labels, max ~5 lines, donuts with ≤3 categories and direct labels.

colors.categoricalNotes: Default palette token set is 'categorical-accent' in mode 'color-blind-safe' (--mic-data-viz-categorical-accent-color-blind-safe-01..08). Alternative modes: michelin-full-colors (#27509b,#d6533c,#1d666f,#7d7300,#982750,#3d7dcd,#e83c42,#4f3704,#77279b,#387dcd), michelin-opt-1, michelin-opt-2 (#004dfc,#722798,...), michelin-dark-mode-opt (#fce500,#d6533c,#7d7300,#004dfc,#e83c42,#3b7dcd), bloom, default, high-contrast, paired (ColorBrewer Paired 12). When no CSS palette var is resolved the chart lib falls back to legacy defaults rgb(39,80,155) #27509b blue, rgb(253,234,51) yellow, rgb(69,185,165) teal, rgb(255,145,0) orange, rgb(64,170,250) light blue, rgb(127,0,224) purple; dark fallback swaps first to rgb(153,206,246) and last to rgb(193,150,240). Pastel palettes (first-palette-recommended: #aae3e2,#c9f4aa,#d9acf5,#fcc2fc,#faf7f0,#fedeff,#ada2ff,#ffc1b6) exist. Guide: 'Do not use colors in addition to those proposed in the design system'; 'use one color per data'.
colors.notes: Sequential default 'oranges' (ColorBrewer Oranges); also 'storm' blues (#b3c7f7,#64b3f3,#009ceb,#0086e5,#0070e0,#0050eb,#0641c8,#0b31a5,#092b85). Diverging default 'rdbu' (ColorBrewer RdBu 11); also 'temperature' (#262a76..#8e1f20) and 'divergent' red-green (#b73a3a..#026545). Fills are drawn with alpha: bars/pies/polar background 0.6 (hover 0.8) with opaque border; line area fill 0.4, opaque line; pie slice borders white. Dark mode: font white, gridlines rgba(255,255,255,0.2), tooltip border rgba(255,255,255,0.3). Do/don't images use a dark charcoal (~#333) for the emphasised bar/slice and mid-greys for others (grey highlight scheme). 'Use colors with high level of contrast to stand out alerts or important information.'

typography.notes: Chart.js title, legend, tick and point-label fonts all forced to family 'Noto Sans'; colour black (white in dark mode) unless ticksColor overridden. Headings in the brand use 'Michelin Unit Titling'. Guide: use at most 2 fonts and 2–3 font sizes; title and subtitle at different sizes; avoid rotating text. Theme body sizes 12–18px, headings 20–36px.

structure.gridlines: Chart.js grid on both scales set to rgba(0,0,0,0.1) (dark: rgba(255,255,255,0.2)); reference images show only faint horizontal gridlines.
structure.axisLine: Chart.js default (thin); example images show no prominent axis lines.
structure.zeroLine: Bar charts must start at 0 baseline ('Truncation leads to misrepresentation').
structure.yAxisTitle: omitted in examples; measure stated in subtitle ('per month')
structure.unitPlacement: abbreviated in tick labels (5k, 10k, 20k) and unit in subtitle
structure.frame: Charts placed in individual cards on a light grey dashboard background.
structure.background: white card on 'unified' light-grey page background
structure.notes: Line charts: 'Use adaptive y-axis scale' (need not start at 0); 'Avoid confusing dual-axis'. Canvas max-height 600px.

legend.placement: top (Chart.js default) – shown above the plot in the anatomy image, left-aligned under the subtitle
legend.directLabels: Preferred for donuts: 'Labeling directly on the chart is super helpful'; legend attached with category AND value.
legend.title: not shown
legend.swatchShape: circle (usePointStyle true, boxWidth 6); line charts use dataset borderColor
legend.notes: Legend hidden unless the legend input is set. 'A chart should always include a title and a legend.' Bubble charts must include a bubble size reference legend.

marks.bars: Equal-width bars, fill at 60% alpha with 1px opaque border of same hue; example shows slightly rounded top corners. Order bars (largest left for vertical, top for horizontal); max 10 bars; horizontal when labels long.
marks.lines: Opaque line, area under line 40% alpha if filled; points filled with series colour and white border, hover point white with coloured border. 'Avoid using smoothed line' (although the anatomy image shows a smoothed curve). 'Avoid to represent more than 5 lines.'
marks.pies: Donut/pie discouraged ('In most cases, a bar chart is a much better option'); fewer than 3 categories, group extra into 'Others', order slices, no labels on top of slices (callout labels outside 'A - 32%'), avoid thin donuts. Slice fill 60% alpha with white borders.
marks.notes: Bubble: area proportional to third variable.

labels.dataLabels: Use only if audience needs them; donut labels outside with leader lines in format 'Category - NN%'.
labels.numberFormat: k abbreviation on axis ticks (5k, 20k) in examples; percent in donut labels
labels.dates: Short month names (Jan, Feb, Mar) in examples
labels.notes: Horizontal axis labels parallel to axis; avoid rotated text; clearly indicate where each axis starts.

furniture.title: Always include a title; title must be 'descriptive and qualitative'; bold title with smaller subtitle stating the measure (e.g. 'Evolution of requests' / 'per month').
furniture.source: 'Look for the source of your data' – no prescribed source line format.

annotations: Highlight a single item (dark charcoal) against greys so 'users understand that category A is the one to get their attention on'; reference line in grey in bar example.
layout: Dashboard: light grey background with one card per visual; use layout to create hierarchy; cards aligned to the column grid. Chart host flex:1, max-height 600px.
interaction: Chart.js tooltips: background rgba(0,0,0,0.8), border rgba(0,0,0,0.1) (dark: rgba(255,255,255,0.3)), title/body text black (white in dark mode) as set by the lib. Hover: bars go to 80% alpha; line points turn white with coloured border. Optional zoom/pan via chartjs-plugin-zoom; chartClick/chartHover outputs. Dark mode via colorMode.
accessibility: Default categorical palette is a colour-blind-safe set; 'high-contrast' mode available. 'Keep accessibility in mind and do use contrasting shades.' Add a physical element in addition to colour for states.

chartTypes.notes: Component library supports bar, line, pie, donut, polar area, radar, bubble, scatter, mixed.

distinctiveRules.rule: All chart text (title, ticks, legend, point labels) is Noto Sans in pure black (white in dark mode).
distinctiveRules.quote: const fontColor = isDark ? 'white' : 'black'; const font = { family: 'Noto Sans' }

distinctiveRules.rule: Gridlines on every cartesian scale are rgba(0,0,0,0.1) (dark mode rgba(255,255,255,0.2)).
Bar, pie and polar fills are the series colour at 60% opacity with a fully opaque 1px border; hover raises fill to 80%.
Pie/donut slices are separated by white borders; line points have white borders.
Legend uses small circular point-style swatches (boxWidth 6) and is hidden unless explicitly enabled.
distinctiveRules.quote: usePointStyle: true, boxWidth: 6 ... if (this.legend === undefined) options.plugins.legend = { display: false }

distinctiveRules.rule: Tooltips are dark translucent boxes rgba(0,0,0,0.8) with a faint border.
Default categorical palette is the 8-colour colour-blind-safe set starting dark teal #074650, teal #009292, pink #fe6db6.
Bar charts always start at a 0 baseline and are sorted, largest on top (horizontal) or left (vertical); max 10 bars.
distinctiveRules.quote: Always start a bar chart at 0 baseline ... place the largest values on top ... shouldn’t have more than 10 bars

distinctiveRules.rule: Use horizontal bars instead of rotating category labels; avoid rotated text generally.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use a horizontal bar chart instead of rotating labels.

distinctiveRules.rule: Line charts: adaptive (non-zero) y-scale allowed, no smoothing, no dual axes, at most 5 lines.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use adaptive y-axis scale ... Avoid using smoothed line. Avoid confusing dual-axis ... Avoid to represent more than 5 lines.

distinctiveRules.rule: Donuts limited to fewer than 3 categories plus 'Others', ordered, thick ring, labels outside with leader lines as 'Category - NN%', never on top of slices.
distinctiveRules.quote: Limit the number of slices ... (less than 3 category of data). Don’t label on top of slices. Thin donut charts are impossible to read.

distinctiveRules.rule: Emphasise one category in dark charcoal and render the rest in mid/light greys.
distinctiveRules.quote: Users understand that category A is the one to get their attention on.

distinctiveRules.rule: Dashboards use a unified light-grey background with each chart in its own white card.
distinctiveRules.quote: We recommend to apply a light grey background. Then you can create cards for each of the visuals

distinctiveRules.rule: Every chart has a bold descriptive title plus a smaller subtitle stating the measure/unit, top-left, and a legend.
distinctiveRules.quote: A chart should always include a title and a legend ... Use title and subtitle with different size of font

distinctiveRules.rule: At most 2 fonts and 2–3 font sizes per report/chart.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use at maximum 2 differents fonts ... Use 2–3 font sizes

referenceImages.describes: Line chart anatomy. Large bold black sans title 'Evolution of requests' top-left, small grey subtitle 'per month' beneath. Legend row under subtitle, left-aligned, with circular swatches: light blue-grey 'Planned' and dark Michelin blue 'Completed', small grey text. Two smoothed lines (dark blue #27509b-like and lighter desaturated blue), ~2px, no markers. Y axis left with grey tick labels 0, 5k, 10k, 15k, 20k; very faint light-grey horizontal gridlines only; no axis lines; x labels Jan–Jul in small grey. No y-axis title, no source, no logo, white background.

'Do' example (green check + green bar header) for starting bars at 0. Vertical bar chart on a very light grey/off-white panel: four wide bars A–D in dark charcoal (#333) with slightly rounded top corners, gaps ~25% of bar width. Y axis 0–500 with light grey tick labels and very faint horizontal gridlines, no axis lines. A thin grey horizontal reference line crosses at ~360. Small grey category labels below bars. No title/legend.

'Do' donut example: thick donut (inner radius ~50%) starting at 12 o'clock, largest slice 'A - 32%' in dark charcoal clockwise first, then B, C, Others, D in mid-grey shades separated by thin white borders. Labels outside the ring in boxed callouts ('A - 32%' black text with black box border; others grey text with grey boxes) connected by thin leader lines. White panel, no legend.
